Modify or Extend Existing RTL:
Align DUT/testbench interfaces first by adding all expected ports/signals (`en`, `op_sel`, `bitwise_op`, status outputs) before behavior tuning.
Keep operation decode mutually exclusive and explicitly clear `overflow` on non-shift modes to avoid stale-status mismatches.
Drive `serial_out` directly from current `q` using `shift_dir` so left/right mode checks stay consistent.
Implement added transforms (arithmetic shift, bitwise ops, reverse, invert) in the same clocked block to match cycle-by-cycle expectations.
Use `en` as a hard state-update gate so disabled-mode checks preserve register/state outputs.
Integrate multiple modules into a top mo:
Fix compile/elaboration blockers first by creating the exact expected top module/file names before functional tuning.
For async unlock/control signals crossing into pclk logic, use a 2-flop synchronizer in the top-level wrapper.
Keep integration changes minimal: preserve submodule interfaces and route existing outputs through the new top-level unchanged.
Implement security gating at the controlled function boundary (history update path) so APB CSR behavior stays backward compatible.
When unlock sequences are pulse-driven, make the FSM resilient to idle cycles and reset only on incorrect write attempts.
Create new RTL from spec:
Create the exact expected top module/file first to clear elaboration blockers before functional tuning.
Implement explicit width selection (8/16/32/64) via `sel` and keep masked/zero-extended payload handling deterministic.
Drive `done` as a clean transaction-complete pulse and keep reset behavior unambiguous across TX/RX state.
Use a simple, test-stable TX/RX handshake path, then layer Gray conversion as `data ^ (data >> 1)` on reconstructed output.
Debug/fix buggy RTL:
Start from the first failing assertion and inspect staged RTL operators first; data-transform bugs often compile but break functional checks.
In true dual-port RAM fixes, keep memory width exactly DATA_WIDTH and remove unintended write/read data mangling (XOR/shift/add/sub).
Use a single posedge sequential process for both ports and keep deterministic same-address write precedence via assignment order.
